    • findType

      public static String findType(int numarg, String pred, KB kb)
      Find the argument type restriction for a given predicate and argument number that is inherited from one of its super-relations. A "+" is appended to the type if the parameter must be a class, meaning that a domainSubclass is defined for this argument in one of the loaded .kif files. Argument number 0 is used for the return type of a Function. Asking for a non-existent arg will return null;

    • winnowTypeList

      public void winnowTypeList(Set<String> types, KB kb)

      Parameters:
      types - A List of classes (class name Strings) that constrain the value of a SUO-KIF variable.
      kb - The KB used to determine if any of the classes in the List types are redundant.

    • findTypeRestrictionsExpr

      public Map<String,Set<String>> findTypeRestrictionsExpr(Expr expr, KB kb)
      Fully Expr-based replacement for {link #findTypeRestrictions(Formula, KB)}.

      No KIF string is ever constructed. Merging logic is identical to the original: domain types are kept for implicitly-typed variables; for explicitly-typed variables only "+" (subclass) markers from either source are retained.

      Was package-private; widened to public so that the trans package (THFnew) can use it directly on Expr trees without converting back to a Formula string.

    • addTypeRestrictionsRecurseExpr

      private Expr addTypeRestrictionsRecurseExpr(Expr expr, Map<String,Set<String>> varmap, KB kb)
      Recursively walk an Expr tree and inject type guards inside quantifier (forall/exists) bodies. This is the Expr-based analogue of
      invalid reference 
      #addTypeRestrictionsRecurse(KB, Formula, StringBuilder)
      .
      • forall (?Z) body with guard G becomes forall (?Z) (=> G body)
      • exists (?Z) body with guard G becomes exists (?Z) (and G body)
      • Other logical operators are recursed into transparently.
      • Simple predicate clauses are returned unchanged.
      Parameters:
      expr - Expr subtree to transform
      varmap - type map for the current lexical scope
      kb - knowledge base (for buildTypeGuardExpr(java.lang.String, java.lang.String, com.articulate.sigma.KB))
      Returns:
      transformed Expr; may be the same object when nothing changed

    • addTypeRestrictionsExpr

      Expr addTypeRestrictionsExpr(Expr expr, Map<String,Set<String>> varmap, KB kb)
      Expr-based equivalent of
      invalid reference 
      #addTypeRestrictions(Formula, KB)
      .

      Wraps the formula with type-guard antecedents for free variables and injects type guards inside quantifier bodies via addTypeRestrictionsRecurseExpr(com.articulate.sigma.parsing.Expr, java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.util.Set<java.lang.String>>, com.articulate.sigma.KB). Returns the original expr reference unchanged when no type restrictions apply, allowing the caller to detect this with reference equality.

      This is intentionally package-private for unit testing.

      Parameters:
      expr - the Expr tree (after variable-arity renaming)
      varmap - type map from findTypeRestrictionsExpr(com.articulate.sigma.parsing.Expr, com.articulate.sigma.KB)
      kb - knowledge base
      Returns:
      type-guarded Expr, or expr itself if nothing changed

    • renameVariableArityInExpr

      private Expr renameVariableArityInExpr(Expr expr, KB kb)
      Recursively rename any VariableArityRelation predicates in an Expr tree by appending the arity suffix __N (or __NFn for function symbols). This mirrors the renaming done in {link #preProcessRecurse} and Formula.renameVariableArityRelations(com.articulate.sigma.KB, java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.String>), but operates directly on the Expr AST without string reconstruction.

    • preProcessExpr

      public Set<Expr> preProcessExpr(Formula formula, boolean isQuery, KB kb)
      Expr-based preprocessing: extended fast path that handles predicate variables (Phase A), row variables (Phase B), and type restrictions (Phase C) entirely within the Expr AST — no string round-trips.

      Phase A — Predicate variable expansion: If fa.predVarCache is non-empty, PredVarInst.processOne(com.articulate.sigma.Formula) instantiates every predicate variable at the Expr level via PredVarInst.substituteVar(com.articulate.sigma.parsing.Expr, java.lang.String, java.lang.String). The result is a set of FormulaASTs, each with a concrete relation in place of each pred-var.

      Phase B — Row variable expansion: For each FormulaAST from Phase A that has row variables, RowVar.expandRowVarExpr(com.articulate.sigma.Formula) splices the expanded argument lists directly into the Expr tree.

      Phase C — Variable-arity renaming + type restrictions: Unchanged from the original no-var fast path.

      Parameters:
      isQuery - true for query mode
      kb - the knowledge base
      fa - the FormulaAST (must have a non-null expr)
      Returns:
      set of preprocessed Expr trees ready for ExprToTPTP.translate(com.articulate.sigma.parsing.Expr, boolean, java.lang.String); empty if pred-var instantiation yields no results

    • preProcessExpr

      public Set<Expr> preProcessExpr(Expr expr, boolean isQuery, KB kb)
      Bridge overload: wraps a bare Expr in a minimal Formula (no pred-var / row-var caches) and delegates to preProcessExpr(Formula, boolean, KB). Keeps existing callers and tests working without change.
      Parameters:
      expr - the Expr tree from Formula.expr
      isQuery - true for query mode
      kb - the knowledge base
      Returns:
      set of preprocessed Expr trees ready for ExprToTPTP.translate(com.articulate.sigma.parsing.Expr, boolean, java.lang.String)
